extraction.name: EuroSAT
extraction.description: A novel dataset based on Sentinel-2 satellite images covering 13 spectral bands and consisting of 10 classes with in total 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced images for land use and land cover classification.
extraction.creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth
extraction.citeAs: Helber, P., Bischke, B., Dengel, A., & Borth, D. (2019). EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. arXiv preprint arXiv:1709.00029v2.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Satellite images taken by Sentinel-2A were downloaded via Amazon S3, focusing on European cities covered in the European Urban Atlas across 34 countries. Images with low cloud levels were selected. Image patches measuring 64x64 pixels were extracted from images recorded throughout the year.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sentinel-2A satellite multi-spectral image data downloaded via Amazon S3.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were extracted as 64x64 pixel patches. For single-band evaluations, bands with lower spatial resolution were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation. The dataset received no atmospheric correction, retaining color casts. Bad patches (clouds, mislabeling, dead pixels, or ice/snow) were manually checked and discarded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Classes were assigned based on the European Urban Atlas mapping guide. Ten land use and land cover classes were selected based on visibility at 10m/pixel resolution. Ground truth was manually checked multiple times and corrected by sorting out mislabeled images and images covered in snow or ice.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Enables Earth observation applications including urban area development, disaster recovery, nature protection, sustainable development, monitoring deforestation (a main contributor to climate change), and updating crowdsourced maps like OpenStreetMap.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The distribution of images across European countries is influenced by the number of represented cities per country in the European Urban Atlas.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has a spatial resolution of 10 to 60 meters per pixel (lower than commercial high-resolution imagery) and does not allow finely graduated per-pixel segmentation. The data has not received atmospheric correction, resulting in color casts. Classifiers sometimes confuse agricultural land classes as well as highway and river classes.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, testing, and benchmarking machine learning models (e.g., CNNs) for land use and land cover classification, land use change detection, and map updating/verification.
